title: Flat dual of the ideal of a section of a nodal family
statement: Let $T$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $\pi:C\to T$ be a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], finitely presented family of nonempty connected reduced nodal curves of pure dimension one [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres]. Let $\Delta:T\to C$ be any section, not required to be smooth, and put $\mathcal J=\ker(\mathcal O_C\to\Delta_*\mathcal O_T)$ and $\mathcal J^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_C}(\mathcal J,\mathcal O_C)$. There is an invertible $\mathcal O_T$-module $\mathcal N$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and a canonical exact sequence $0\to\mathcal O_C\xrightarrow{\mathrm{mult}}\mathcal J^\vee\to\Delta_*\mathcal N\to0$, with $\mathcal N=\Delta^*(\mathcal J^\vee/\mathcal O_C)$, where the first arrow sends a local function to multiplication on $\mathcal J$. The module $\mathcal J^\vee$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent] and of finite presentation (locally the cokernel of a map between finite rank free modules) and flat over $T$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Formation of $\mathcal J$, $\mathcal J^\vee$, $\mathcal N$, the multiplication arrow and this exact sequence commutes with arbitrary base change on $T$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-module-pullback], naturally in isomorphisms of pointed families. On a geometric fibre $C_\Omega$, if $x=\Delta(\Omega)$ is smooth, the multiplier interpretation identifies $\mathcal J^\vee_\Omega$ with $\mathcal O_{C_\Omega}(x)$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. If $x$ is a node and $\nu:\widetilde C_\Omega\to C_\Omega$ is the partial normalization separating just that node (finite, an isomorphism off $x$, with the two normalized branches over $x$) [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], then the same multiplier interpretation identifies $\mathcal J^\vee_\Omega$ with $\nu_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde C_\Omega}$.

source.place: Main Lemma; Proposition 3.1, Corollary 3.2 and Section 4, especially J dual/R = A via the class of epsilon. Arbitrary-base finite-presentation version of the noetherian statement, and smooth/nodal geometric-fibre multiplier descriptions. Local PDF WANTED; arXiv v2 consulted online.

proof.text: Properness includes separatedness. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion] makes $\Delta$ a closed immersion. Its ideal $\mathcal J$ is quasi-coherent, with the stated affine kernel description, by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Off its image $\mathcal J=\mathcal O_C$, so its dual and multiplication map are the identity there. All subsequent assertions can therefore be checked near section points.

At a section point smooth in its fibre, [lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion] applies because $\pi$ is flat and locally finitely presented; shrink to a smooth relative curve neighbourhood. Apply [lem-sc-smooth-section-affine-coordinates] with $d=1$: over an affine base $\operatorname{Spec}A$ it gives an etale, flat map $A[z]\to B$, with $\mathcal J=(z)B$ and $B/zB=A$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_B(zB,B)=z^{-1}B$ as multiplier modules, multiplication embeds $B$, and its quotient is $z^{-1}B/B\simeq B/zB=A$. Here $z^{-1}B$ denotes the free rank-one fractional module generated by $1/z$. These formulas persist for every $A\to A'$: by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] the map $A'[z]\to B'=A'\otimes_A B$ is etale, hence flat by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat], so multiplication by $z$ stays injective and $B'/zB'=A'$. The comparison of duals sends $1/z$ to $1/z$.

source.place: Tag 01V9, lemma-smooth-at-point; Tag 054L, lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space; Tag 02GO, lemma-base-change-etale; centred section coordinates

proof.text: At a nonsmooth section point apply [lem-trf-nodal-family-etale-local-model]. Its hypotheses are precisely flatness, local finite presentation and pure one-dimensional nodal geometric fibres. Write its model as $W=\operatorname{Spec}_V(\mathcal O_V[u,v]/(uv-h))$, with etale maps $V\to T$, $U\to C$ and $U\to W$. The induced $U\to C_V$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], since $C_V\to C$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Pull $U\to C_V$ back along $\Delta_V$ and use the resulting etale neighbourhood $V'\to V$ as base. The tautological lift of $\Delta$ is now a section of $U_{V'}\to V'$. On affine neighbourhoods of the chosen points, let $a,b$ be the values of $u,v$ on this section. Evaluating $uv=h$ gives $h=ab$. The model ring is therefore $R=A[u,v]/(uv-ab)$ for $V'=\operatorname{Spec}A$.

Arrange that both etale maps from the source chart, to the original base-changed curve and to $\operatorname{Spec}R$, are separated by restricting to affine neighbourhoods. The inverse image of either section is then a separated etale scheme over the base containing the chosen lifted section. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion] this chosen section is clopen in each inverse image. Each inverse image is closed in the chart: the original section is closed by Step 1 and the model section has ideal $(u-a,v-b)$. Remove the two closed complements of the chosen section and refine by affine opens, shrinking the base to keep the chosen section. Both inverse images now equal this section as schemes. Consequently on the resulting chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$ the actual pulled ideal is exactly $IB$, where $I=(u-a,v-b)\subset R$ and $R\to B$ is etale. All removals retain the chosen point; such charts cover the section etale locally.

source.place: Tag 024T, proposition-properties-sections; isolation of the lifted section in each closed inverse image

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-node-section-dual-presentation] to $A,a,b,R,I$. It gives finite presentations of $I$ and $M=\operatorname{Hom}_R(I,R)$, generators $\mathbf1,e$, relations $a\mathbf1+(u-a)e=0$ and $-v\mathbf1+(v-b)e=0$, and $0\to R\mathbf1\to M\to A\to0$, with quotient $r\mathbf1+se\mapsto\epsilon(s)$. The quotient is killed by $I$. The same node's flat-extension clause applies to $R\to B$, which is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]. Thus the chart ideal and its actual dual are finitely presented, and multiplication gives an injection $B\to\operatorname{Hom}_B(IB,B)$ with quotient $B/IB=A$. No Noetherian assumption, regularity of $a$ or $b$, or smoothness of the section is used.

source.place: Section 3, Proposition 3.1; split-hyperbola presentation of the existing algebra node

proof.text: For flatness in a nodal model put $w=u+v-a-b$. Substituting $v=w-u+a+b$ gives $R\simeq A[w][u]/(u^2-(w+a+b)u+ab)$, free with basis $1,u$ over $A[w]$ by division by this monic polynomial. Thus $R$ is $A$-free. The quotient map $M\to A$ of [lem-sfb-split-node-section-dual-presentation] has the $A$-linear section $c\mapsto ce$, so $M\simeq R\oplus A$ as $A$-modules. This is $A$-free too: tensoring an injection with it is a direct sum of copies of that injection. The chart dual $B\otimes_RM$ is $A$-flat: its tensor on an $A$-module $L$ is $B\otimes_R(M\otimes_A L)$, and [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] applies to the flat $R$-module $B$. On a smooth chart the dual is free of rank one over $B$, which is $A$-flat since $A\to B$ is the given flat curve chart; off the section it is $\mathcal O_C$.

source.place: Section 3, explicit polynomial normal form and quotient; agent argument deriving relative flatness without completion

proof.text: First descend finite presentation of $\mathcal J$. Its quasi-coherence is Step 1, and its pullbacks to all the charts in Steps 2--5 are finitely presented. On each affine open of $C$, refine this covering to a finite affine etale cover using [new-etale-finite-affine-cech-basis]; the disjoint union is an affine faithfully flat cover by [lem-sc-etale-standard-cover-cech]. Finite presentation descends by [lem-pc-fpqc-descent](2). Now [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-hom-finite-presentation-quasi-coherent] shows $\mathcal J^\vee$ is quasi-coherent. The actual pullback of this dual to any chart equals its chart dual by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-hom-finitely-presented]: the source module is finitely presented and the chart map is flat. Applying the same fpqc descent again proves finite presentation of $\mathcal J^\vee$. In particular the descended property is finite presentation on neighbourhoods, not merely at individual stalks.

source.place: Tags 023T and 05B0, lemma-finite-presentation-descends; Schemes Section 01LA(10); More on Algebra Tag 087R(1)

proof.text: The multiplication map is injective. On each affine open use Step 7's faithfully flat affine cover. Flat pullback takes the kernel to the zero kernel of the chart multiplication maps; the fpqc equivalence of [lem-pc-fpqc-descent](1) reflects the zero module, so this kernel vanishes. Form its cokernel $Q=\mathcal J^\vee/\mathcal O_C$. It is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image]. The local calculations give $\mathcal JQ=0$, and therefore [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-annihilated](2) identifies $Q$ canonically with $\Delta_*\Delta^*Q$. Put $\mathcal N=\Delta^*Q$. On each etale base neighbourhood used above it is $\mathcal O_T$, because $B/IB=A$ in the nodal case and $B/zB=A$ in the smooth case. Finite local freeness of rank one descends by [lem-pc-fpqc-descent](2), applied on each affine open of $T$ to a finite affine etale refinement of these base neighbourhoods given by [new-etale-finite-affine-cech-basis], whose disjoint union is a faithfully flat affine cover by [lem-sc-etale-standard-cover-cech]. Thus $\mathcal N$ is invertible and the claimed exact sequence is established. For relative flatness take a chart point $z$ over $t_1\in T_1$ and $t\in T$, where $T_1\to T$ is the etale base neighbourhood in Steps 2--4. Step 6 makes the dual stalk at $z$ flat over $\mathcal O_{T_1,t_1}$. By [lem-trf-etale-local-ring-flatness] it is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$. The composite chart map to $C$ is etale, hence flat, so [lem-trf-relative-flatness-source-cover] descends this flatness to the corresponding stalk on $C$. These charts cover the section; off it the dual is $\mathcal O_C$, flat over $T$ by hypothesis.

proof.text: Let $T'\to T$ be arbitrary. Base change the charts of Steps 2--4; they still give an etale cover by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. On a nodal chart the model becomes $R'=A'[u,v]/(uv-a'b')$ and $B'=A'\otimes_A B$ is flat over $R'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]. Both coefficient-change and flat-extension clauses of [lem-sfb-split-node-section-dual-presentation] apply. For the ideal their composite is $A'\otimes_A IB\simeq B'\otimes_{R'}I'\simeq I'B'$, taking $c\otimes j$ to the actual pulled-back function $cj$. For the dual the two paths through $A'\otimes_A M$, $B'\otimes_{R'}\operatorname{Hom}_{R'}(I',R')$, and $\operatorname{Hom}_{B'}(I'B',B')$ agree: on a simple tensor the comparison sends $c\otimes\phi$ to the map $d\otimes i\mapsto cd\otimes\phi(i)$. In particular it takes $\mathbf1,e$ to their primed maps and takes the quotient to $B'/I'B'=A'$. The same statements on smooth charts are the $1/z$ calculation of Step 2. Off the section they are identities. Thus the canonical comparisons for $\mathcal J$, $\mathcal J^\vee$ and multiplication are isomorphisms, and the pulled sequence is exact on every chart, hence on $C_{T'}$. This proves arbitrary, including nonflat, base change; generic flat-Hom base change alone would not prove it.

source.place: Section 3, Proposition 3.1, and Section 4; explicit comparison via polynomial presentations over arbitrary rings

proof.text: Cokernels and module pullbacks give the canonical comparison for $Q$ from Step 9. The identification $Q=\Delta_*\mathcal N$ is compatible with this comparison: for the closed immersion $\Delta$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change] identifies its pushforward after every base change, and the adjunction unit in [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-annihilated] is the quotient map $Q\to Q/\mathcal JQ$ on affines. Pulling it back along the section therefore gives exactly the comparison for $\mathcal N=\Delta^*Q$. For a further base change, the formula on simple tensors in Step 9 is unchanged after either order of substitution. An isomorphism of pointed families carries the kernel ideal to the kernel ideal, the map $\phi$ to its conjugate, and multiplication to multiplication. It consequently carries the cokernel and its section pullback to the corresponding objects. This proves the asserted naturality without choosing a global generator of $\mathcal N$.

After a geometric base change, Step 9 identifies the dual with the dual of the actual point ideal. If the point $x$ is smooth, its ideal is the invertible Cartier ideal of $x$ by [lem-trf-smooth-curve-section-cartier], applied to a smooth open neighbourhood of $x$ over the geometric field. By [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] its inverse is $\mathcal O(x)$. The local identification is $zB\mapsto z^{-1}B$ by multiplication. Off $x$ it is the identity. These agree in the total quotient rings and give the claimed global multiplier identification.

source.place: Tag 067R, lemma-section-smooth-regular-immersion; divisor inverse module and multiplier description

proof.text:
Suppose instead $x$ is a node of the geometric fibre $D$. By [lem-trf-nodal-normalization-quotient] its full normalization has quotient $ igoplus_{y	ext{ node}}k_y$ over $\mathcal O_D$. On a neighbourhood excluding the other finitely many nodes, the partial normalization at $x$ is the full normalization, so its quotient is $k_x$; away from $x$ it is the identity. Thus $0	o\mathcal O_D	o
u_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde D}	o k_x	o0$. Write $\mathfrak m$ for the point ideal. Since $\mathfrak m k_x=0$, multiplication gives $
u_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde D}	o\mathcal Hom(\mathfrak m,\mathcal O_D)$. This is injective: Step 8 gives $\operatorname{Ann}(\mathfrak m)=0$. If a normalization multiplier $q=c/s$ (with $s$ a non-zero-divisor) kills $\mathfrak m$, then $cj=0$ in the local curve ring for every $j\in\mathfrak m$, hence $c=0$ and $q=0$. Step 8 on this geometric base gives $\mathcal Hom(\mathfrak m,\mathcal O_D)/\mathcal O_D\simeq k_x$. The induced map between the two quotient copies of $k_x$ is injective: a multiplier mapping into $\mathcal O_D$ differs from that function by a multiplier killing $\mathfrak m$, hence is that function by the same calculation. It is therefore an isomorphism, and so is the map of middle modules. This is exactly the multiplier identification with $
u_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde D}$.
